messages:
customer-jane: Hey team — we're seeing SSE streams cut off after ~2 minutes of idle. Client gets 1–3 events then connection closes and user sees a 502 from the ALB. This started after a config change last week.

customer-jane: Quick repro: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?user=123` — I can reproduce reliably if I let the stream sit idle for ~120s, first chunk delivered then connection drops.

alice: Thanks, sorry about this. Can you share the X-Request-ID from the failing request and any ALB/NGINX error lines? Also whether traffic goes through Cloudflare/CF proxy or directly to ALB.

customer-jane: X-Request-ID: 8f3b2c9a. Stack: Cloudflare (w/ proxying) -> ALB -> nginx (origin) -> redwood app. ALB logs show `elb_status_code=502; target_status_code=200; target: http 200 but connection closed` — nginx error: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.3, server: _, request: "GET /v1/stream?user=123 HTTP/1.1"`

ben: That pattern (target 200 + elb 502 + upstream prematurely closed) smells like an idle/tcp half-close between ALB and origin or premature upstream close. Default ALB idle timeout is 60s, but Cloudflare can reset/h2 translate. Do you have any app-level keepalive/heartbeat?

customer-jane: App sends periodic SSE comment lines as keepalive every 30s (`: keepalive

`). We still see the cut after ~120s. No token rotation during the window.

chris: Two quick hypotheses: 1) ALB idle timeout vs nginx `proxy_read_timeout` mismatch, ALB may see no data from client-facing side if Cloudflare does some HTTP/2 reprioritization; 2) nginx proxy_buffering or chunked encoding being rewritten causing upstream to flush/close.

chris: Can you try a quick nginx staging tweak (if safe) — add this to the streaming location and redeploy to test: 

```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";   # clear Connection to avoid upstream close
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  send_timeout 3600s;
}
```

support-ops: Also double-check ALB idle timeout in the target group -> set to > 300s for long-lived streams. If Cloudflare sits in front, check their `proxy_read_timeout` equivalent and disable `origin_connection_timeout` shrink.

customer-jane: Pushed the nginx change to staging, retried and able to keep stream open for 10+ minutes with the same curl repro. Production still failing though. Production ALB idle timeout currently 60s.

alice: Ok that narrows it. Two action items: 1) Increase ALB idle timeout to 300s for the streaming listeners (we can do this during a maintenance window). 2) Schedule a brief test to route a client directly to ALB bypassing Cloudflare to confirm CF involvement.

ben: I'll open an infra ticket to bump the ALB idle timeout for streaming TG: ENG-STREAM-324. Assigning to @ben and @chris to follow up on Cloudflare header passthrough.

ingress-bot: Ticket ENG-STREAM-324 created by ben — prod ALB idle timeout change requested. Please include maintenance window and rollback plan.

customer-jane: One more oddity — when some clients reconnect after the 502 they briefly get 401s and then full responses, causing duplicate billing usage spikes. Could be token refresh race. We saw `401 unauthorized` in our client logs immediately after reconnect, then `200` on retry.

chris: That points to reconnect flow/short-lived token + client retry logic. If the client retries with the same token while server rotated it, you'll see transient 401s and duplicate usage on successful retry. Please collect client retry timestamps and correlate with our access logs (X-Request-ID).

support-ops: For triage next steps: (1) change ALB idle timeout to 300s temporarily, (2) deploy nginx proxy_buffering off in prod streaming location (safe toggle), (3) run a Canary with CF bypass to see if behavior persists, (4) collect pcap/flow logs for a failing session and attach to ENG ticket.

customer-jane: Will schedule a 10m canary window and attach logs. Attaching a sample nginx error + ALB log in thread: `nginx_err: 2026/03/16 14:08:22 [error] 12345#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.3, server: _, request: "GET /v1/stream?..."` and `alb: 2026-03-16T14:08:22.123Z elb_status_code=502 target_status_code=200 target_response_time=18.3`

alice: Perfect. Once ENG-STREAM-324 has pcap + logs we'll triage kernel/TCP RST timing. If we see FIN/RST from ALB side at ~120s, that's the smoking gun.

ben: FYI workaround for clients: implement application-level heartbeats (send a lightweight SSE comment every 20s) and client-side exponential reconnect jitter to avoid thundering reconnections if multiple clients get cut.

customer-jane: Thanks all — starting the canary in 15m, will post results + X-Request-IDs for failed sessions. :thumbsup:

support-ops: Great — keep us posted. If you hit a regression or see a 5xx spike, ping #eng-oncall.
